pass_a_gloss: And so someone of the foremost martyrs, having somewhat more than many martyrs the love of learning in Christ, will go up beyond and more quickly. But to you, holy Ambrose, having looked closely in a searching way into a gospel voice, it is open to see that then perhaps either no one of those ever or quite few will hit upon a pouring out of blessedness, a chosen one and more; in which you also will be, if you swim across the contest without doubting. The sayings stand so: Peter once said to the saviour: behold, we let go all things and went after you; what then will be ours. And Jesus said to them, plainly to the apostles: amen I say to you that you who went after me, in the rebirth, when God takes his seat on a throne of his glory, you also will take seats on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel; and each one who let go brothers or sisters or parents or offspring or lands or dwellings on account of my name will take manifold and will inherit life everlasting. On account of these sayings I would have prayed, having acquired on earth as many things as you hold, or more than these, to become a witness in Christ to God, so that I might take manifold or, as Mark says, a hundredfold, which things are much more, the few things, of the kind we will leave behind if we are called to martyrdom, being made a hundredfold. On account of this, if I bear witness, I was wishing also to leave behind offspring with lands and dwellings, so that also beside the God and father of our lord Jesus Christ, out of whom every fatherhood in heavens and on earth takes its name, I might be styled father of manifold and holier offspring, or, so that I speak definitely, hundredfold ones. And if indeed there are fathers, about whom it was said to Abraham: and you will go off toward your fathers with peace, reared in a fine old age, someone might say (I do not know if speaking truth) perhaps those are fathers having once borne witness and having let go offspring, in return for which they have become fathers of fathers, of the patriarch Abraham and other such patriarchs; for it is likely that those having let go offspring and having borne witness become fathers not of babies but of fathers.
pass_b_english: And so one of the foremost martyrs, who has a greater love of learning in Christ than many martyrs, will rise further and sooner. But you, holy Ambrose, if you look carefully into a saying of the Gospel, can see that perhaps either no one who has ever lived, or very few, will attain an outpouring of blessedness that is exceptional and greater; and you too will be in such blessedness, if you swim through the contest without wavering. The words run like this. Peter once said to the Saviour: “Look, we have left everything and followed you; what then will there be for us?” (Matthew 19:27). And Jesus said to them (to the apostles, clearly): “Truly I tell you that you who have followed me, in the regeneration, when God sits on the throne of his glory, you too will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. And everyone who has left brothers or sisters or parents or children or fields or houses for the sake of my name will receive many times as much and will inherit eternal life” (Matthew 19:28-29).

Because of these sayings I would have prayed, had I acquired as much on earth as you have, or even more, to become a martyr to God in Christ, so that I might receive “many times as much”, or, as Mark says, “a hundredfold” (Mark 10:30). That is far more, since the few things we leave behind, if we are called to martyrdom, are multiplied a hundred times. For this reason, if I bear witness, I would wish to leave children behind too, along with fields and houses, so that with the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, “from whom every fatherhood in heaven and on earth is named” (Ephesians 3:15), I might be called the father of many times more children, and holier ones, or, to put it precisely, a hundred times more.

If indeed there are fathers, those of whom it was said to Abraham, “But you will go to your fathers in peace, nourished in a good old age” (Genesis 15:15), someone might say (I do not know whether truly) that perhaps those fathers are men who once bore witness and left their children behind, and in return have become fathers of fathers: of the patriarch Abraham and of other patriarchs like him. For it is likely that those who left their children and bore witness become fathers not of infants but of fathers.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 14); the old English was a digest. The old English split this chapter across sections 13 and 14, garbled its first sentence on the foremost martyrs, and hung an Ephesians 3:15 citation on the closing line about fathers of fathers.
κληρονομησείς read κληρονομήσει; xIndauer read κληθῶμεν; χρηματίco read χρηματίσω; οὡς ἄρα read ὡς ἄρα; φωνὴ read φωνῇ; 7 καὶ read ἢ καὶ.
Koetschau inserts ἃ by conjecture; translated with it, and ὀλίγων ... ἑκατονταπλασιαζομένων taken as a genitive absolute ('since the few things ... are multiplied a hundred times').
Printed text followed: 'you too will be in such blessedness'. Koetschau suspects ὁποίοις ('among whom', the few).
'Fatherhood', not 'family', to keep Origen's play on fathers.
'A martyr to God in Christ', taking τῷ θεῷ as dative of the one witnessed to.
